content: The combination of pseudoephedrine, a decongestant, and triprolidine, an antihistamine, is used to alleviate symptoms such as itchy and watery eyes, sneezing, and a runny or congested nose caused by hay fever, allergies, or the common cold. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other purposes. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. This medication is available in various forms, including capsules, tablets, extended-release capsules, and liquid, all of which are taken orally. It is typically taken every 4 to 6 hours or every 12 hours for the extended-release capsules, depending on your needs. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. Swallow extended-release capsules whole; do not open or crush them. This medication should not be given to children under 12 years of age unless specifically directed by a doctor. Before taking pseudoephedrine and triprolidine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to either of these drugs or any other medications. Do not take this medication if you have used an MAO inhibitor in the past two weeks. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your surgeon or dentist that you are taking this medication. Be aware that this drug may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can increase the sedative effects of this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. This medication may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take it with food or milk. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Mild side effects include dry mouth, nose, and throat; upset stomach; difficulty sleeping; chest congestion; headache; diarrhea; and drowsiness. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects include muscle weakness, vision problems, skin rash, unusual excitement, difficulty breathing, rapid heartbeat, tremors, painful or difficult urination, and hallucinations. If you experience any of these severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately. You or your doctor may report serious side effects to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share it with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. This medication is sold under brand names such as Actifed®, Allerfrim®, and Triafed®.
